name: Dango
description:
Dango turns the AI agent you already use into a presentation designer.

Connect it once, then ask for a deck in the chat you were already having. Dango reads your website to build a brand kit (your colors, your type, your logo, the way you write), and every slide comes out in it. Ask for a pitch deck and it works to a researched spine for that kind of deck, asks you the handful of questions no data can answer, and tells you where a number is missing instead of inventing one.

What comes back is not an export. Every slide is a canvas of individually movable objects, so you can open it in the browser and drag, rewrite or restyle anything by hand, then go back to the same chat and ask for the next change.

Charts and tables draw a stored dataset rather than carrying numbers of their own, so a chart and the table beside it cannot disagree, and correcting a figure once fixes every object that draws it.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Dango to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Dango to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.trydango.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Dango MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dango lists 28 MCP tools, including add_canvas_slide, add_layout, add_object, add_slide, check_slide_fit, create_dataset, create_deck, create_image_upload, critique_deck, delete_object, delete_slide, and duplicate_slide.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Dango?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Dango in productivity on the Manufact MCP catalog include Autodesk Product Help, BoardWise, FlagStat, Keenable Web Search, and PomoDial.
Dango requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Dango is developed by Dango. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
